sentences.text: Dharmpal vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2023

Author: Krishan Pahal
Bench: Krishan Pahal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 83
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 21818 of 2020
Applicant :- Dharmpal

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ram Shiromani Yadav,Ved Mani Sharma
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Bal Krishna Yadav
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
Learned counsel for the informant is not present.
2. Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

3. Heard Shri Ved Mani Sharma, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Shri V.K.S. Parmar,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
4.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.32 of 2019, under Sections 498A, 323, 304-B I.P.C. & 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Cantt, District Bareilly, during the pendency of trial.
5. As per prosecution story, the marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the daughter of the informant as per Hindu Rites in the year 2018.

The applicant and other family members are stated to have demanded dowry from her and as such are stated to have subjected her to cruelty leading to Dharmpal vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130913364/
1 her death on 02.01.2019.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case owing to his relation with the deceased person.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
The parties has agreed to not proceed any further and there is a compromise on record, which is filed as annexure no.7 to the affidavit accompanying the bail application.
The FIR is delayed by about one month and three days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

Learned counsel has further stated that the said fact stands falsified by the fact that the other family members of the informant were present at the stage of inquest proceedings that was undertaken on 03.01.2019 itself.

The panch witnesses of the inquest report are Leeladhar,
who is the brother-in-law of the informant, Jitendra and Vishal Kumar.
Learned counsel has further stated that the presence of three witnesses of the family of the informant indicates that the said compromise was entered into between the parties.
Two witnesses of fact have been examined and they have reiterated the allegations levelled in the FIR.
Learned counsel has indicated several inconsistencies in the statements of the said witnesses.
There is no likelihood of early conclusion of trial in near future.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 31.03.2019.

In case,
the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.

8. The Apex Court in the case of Union of India vs. K.A. Najeeb, AIR 2021 SC 712, has observed as under:-
"We are conscious of the fact that the charges levelled against the respondent are grave and a serious threat to societal harmony.

entities.text: Union of India vs. K.A. Najeeb, AIR 2021 SC 712
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Had it been a case at the threshold,
we would have outrightly turned down the respondent's prayer.

However, keeping in mind the length of the period spent by him in custody and the unlikelihood of the trial being completed anytime soon, the High Court appears to have been left with no other option except to grant bail."

9. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, taking into consideration the fact that there is a compromise entered into between the parties on 02.01.2019 itself and also that there is an inordinate delay in lodging of the FIR, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

10. Let the applicant- Dharmpal involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.

Dharmpal vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130913364/
2
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii). The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
(iv) The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected of the commission of which he is suspected.

(v) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
11. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

12. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

Order Date :- 16.2.2023 Ravi Kant  Dharmpal vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130913364/
